title: APT (Advanced Package Tool)
definition: The primary package manager used by Debian-based Linux distributions (like Ubuntu and Mint). It handles installing, updating, and removing software and automatically resolves dependencies.
simpleExplanation: The App Store for Ubuntu. If you want a program, you don't go to a website to download an `.exe` file. You ask `apt` to find it, download it, and install it automatically.
realWorldExample: You want to install Python. You type `sudo apt update` to refresh the store's catalog, then type `sudo apt install python3`. It automatically downloads Python and the 15 invisible libraries Python needs to function.

basic: What command do you run to upgrade all installed software on your Ubuntu system to the latest versions?
intermediate: Why do you almost always have to run `apt update` BEFORE you run `apt install`?

answers.question: Why update first?
answers.answer: `apt update` doesn't actually update your software. It updates the *catalog index* of what software exists in the world. If you don't update the catalog, `apt install` might try to download a version of a package that was deleted from the internet years ago.
